context.body: David was told, “Behold, the Philistines are fighting against Keilah, and are robbing the threshing floors.”.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: David twice inquires before striking the Philistines, saves Keilah, then learns that its leaders would surrender him and departs into wilderness strongholds.
observations.label: David rescues Keilah and must leave it: textual observation

observations.body: The passage keeps David, his men, Abiathar, Saul, Keilah, and the Philistines, Keilah and the wilderness of Ziph, inquiring, rescuing, plotting, consulting, dispersing, and hiding visible within David's story or later memory.
observations.label: David rescues Keilah and must leave it: action, promise, or consequence

payload.posture: Read 1 Samuel 23:1–14 as its own flight, covenant, and restraint David setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The source places a rescued city cannot become secure refuge inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
